items.title: 2.9 Electronic configuration of ions and free radicals

source_refs.note: Topic 2.9, printed page 40: the heading topic for 2.9.1 and 2.9.2.

blocks.text: Atoms become ions by losing or gaining electrons, and some species carry unpaired electrons; their configurations follow from the atom's. The next two topics treat ions and free radicals.

blocks.prompt: Before reading on, predict the configuration of Mg2+ and of F- from those of the atoms.
blocks.explanation: Magnesium is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2; losing the two 3s electrons gives Mg2+ as 1s2 2s2 2p6. Fluorine is 1s2 2s2 2p5; gaining one electron gives F- as 1s2 2s2 2p6. Both ions have the configuration of neon.

items: Ions and free radicals are described by configurations derived from the atom's: remove electrons for cations, add for anions, and look for unpaired electrons in radicals.
